why: Both move the same single call the same way with equal fidelity, but A's system-level work is deeper and more correctly executed: the cache fix moves only the volatile {date}/{time} line and leaves the authored prompt as a stable front prefix, where B relocates the entire system prompt behind the history for the same saving and a larger behavioural shift, and A built and measured the app's biggest dollar lever (a ~148x cheaper default for a brevity-optimised banter bot) that B deferred unmeasured. A also verified more (17 live runs, text and image through on_message on every branch, cross-vendor fallback actually serving, Flex tier under a models list that B flagged as unmeasured); B's edge is real but narrower — a visible-failure notice A never considered, and a Router-served Claude proposal that touches an actually-configured model.
A_best: The cache-prefix fix is the surgically correct version — split the prompt by line, keep the operator's stable text as a byte-identical front prefix and ride the timestamp last — measured live at 0→3,840 cached tokens and $0.0148→$0.0045 on turn two, paired with the one improvement (cheap default, $0.01336 vs $0.00009 for three on-voice replies) that an expert would push hardest for a Discord banter bot replaying 25 messages per mention.
B_best: i3: a visible failure notice, correctly scoped — generic text so provider errors can't leak model ids or prompt content into a channel, its own try/except, not appended to response_msgs so the node bookkeeping survives — closing the silent-failure gap that Router's spend caps, 402s and 429s make worse, which A left open even after naming it.
A_worst: The cache fix rewrites a user-authored string line by line (collapsing blank runs, emitting two system messages and lifting the date/time out of its authored context), and i4's quality case for changing what every user sees rests on three sampled replies — flagged honestly, but thin for the item A pushes hardest.
B_worst: The app's largest recurring cost — gpt-5.5 at $5/$30 with effort high for a bot told to be brief — is left as an unmeasured needs-decision, so the one item with the biggest dollar leverage ships as prose; and i2's own loses admit the Flex-tier interaction went unmeasured where A simply measured it.
